issue.title: TUI modals bind bare uppercase keys without shift+letter twins, dead under CSI-u key reporting
issue.description:
Roughly 27 ACE TUI modal/pane modules bind bare uppercase mnemonic keys (for
example `("K", ...)`, `("D", ...)`, `("A", ...)`) without the paired
`shift+<letter>` alias that this codebase's own convention requires (see
`G`/`shift+g` in `procs_pane.py` + `TaskList`, `Y`/`shift+y` and `Z`/`shift+z`
in `repo_preview_modal.py`/`glossary_preview_modal.py`/`preview_panel_modal.py`,
and `shift+n` in `preview_panel_modal.py`).

Textual's extended-key parser (`textual/_xterm_parser.py`,
`_sequence_to_key_events`) always lowercases the letter and prefixes modifiers
when a terminal reports a shifted letter as a CSI-u sequence, so those events
arrive as key `"shift+k"` etc. and a bare `("K", ...)` binding never matches.
Terminals/muxers that re-encode shifted letters this way (tmux with
`extended-keys on/always`, foot, WezTerm/Ghostty CSI-u modes) therefore get
silent dead keys for every unpaired uppercase binding, while kitty-direct and
legacy terminals deliver plain text `"K"` and work.

Verified empirically against the installed Textual 8.0.1:
`XTermParser().feed("\x1b[107;2u")` and `feed("\x1b[75;2u")` both yield key
`shift+k` (character None), while `feed("K")` yields key `K`.

Affected files (audited 2026-09-04 by scanning `src/sase/ace/tui/modals/*.py`
for single-uppercase binding keys with no matching `shift+<lower>` twin):
agent_cleanup_panel_modal (C, D, K); artifact_files_modal (+ rendering) (A, Y);
axe_entry_editor_modal, config_edit_modal, config_pane_widget,
custom_gate_modal, gate_action_output_modal, statistics_help_modal,
launch_approval_modal (G); disabled_provider_launch_modal (A); gate_debug_modal
(G, Y); gate_retry_modal (R); mentor_review_modal (A, K, N, P);
models_panel_selector_builder (E, J, K, W); models_panel (H);
notification_modal (M, R, S, V, Y); plan_approval_gate_data (G, Y);
plugins_browser_pane (A, H, I, U); prompt_submit_choice_modal (X);
stashed_prompts_modal (D); update_panel (A, E, P, S); user_question_modal (S);
xprompt_browser_pane (E); zoom_panel_modal (E, G, H, L); zoom_panel_search (E).
(`procs_pane.py` (D, K) is being fixed separately by the tale plan
"Fix silent no-op K (kill) keymap on the Admin Center Procs tab".)

The fix is mechanical: for each bare uppercase binding add the
`("shift+<letter>", same_action, same_description)` twin (and mirror any
`on_key` checks that compare `event.key` to the bare uppercase form, as the
existing `event.key in ("G", "shift+g")` handlers already do). Consider a small
shared helper or a lint/test that asserts every single-uppercase binding key in
`src/sase/ace/tui` has its shift twin, so new modals cannot regress.

task_type_fields.impact: Every unpaired uppercase keymap in those modals is silently dead for users on CSI-u key-reporting terminal stacks; the same defect class already bit the Procs pane's K (kill) key.
task_type_fields.location: src/sase/ace/tui/modals/*.py BINDINGS lists (~27 modules, see description)
task_type_fields.repro: In a terminal that reports shifted letters as CSI-u (e.g. tmux extended-keys on), open any listed modal and press an unpaired uppercase key such as M in the notification modal; the bound action never fires. Parser-level: uv run python -c 'from textual._xterm_parser import XTermParser; print([e.key for e in XTermParser().feed("\x1b[75;2u")])' prints ["shift+k"], which no bare ("K", ...) binding matches.
